_comment: Configured for 'Averaging Periodograms, Smoothing a Periodogram, and Multitaper Estimation Are One Estimator' (paper/main.tex), a methods/tutorial paper for IEEE Transactions on Biomedical Engineering (alternative: J. Neuroscience Methods).
paper_type: Methods / tutorial paper with an exact mathematical identity, quantitative comparisons on simulated and real EEG data, and a practical recipe
field: Biomedical signal processing / nonparametric spectral estimation / clinical EEG
style_guide: IEEE TBME regular paper: abstract, introduction, methods/theory sections, results, discussion/conclusion, appendices allowed. Aimed at neuroscientists and biomedical engineers who use spectral estimation but are not signal-processing specialists; equations kept to a minimum in the body, proofs in appendices.
custom_notes: The central claims are (i) Thomson's 1982 eq. (8.3): the eigenvalue-weighted all-taper multitaper estimate equals the box-smoothed periodogram exactly; (ii) it also equals the average of periodograms of a sinc window slid one sample at a time (exact in the limit of a long window, error ~1/L); (iii) every quadratic estimator is a bank of tapers with weights whose flatness sets the degrees of freedom; (iv) the everyday K-taper estimator is the leaky estimate minus its leaky remainder, and tapering before smoothing/averaging is the practical substitute, at a quantified variance cost.

All numbers in the paper are produced by the accompanying repository (specsmooth Python package, demos/make_figures.py, demos/band_power_table.py, tests/). The truthfulness and reproducibility agents should check claims against that code.

Do not penalize the pedagogical tone or the use of appendices for proofs; that is deliberate. Do flag any place where the exposition overstates novelty relative to Thomson (1982), Welch (1967), Nuttall & Carter (1982), Riedel & Sidorenko (1995), Bronez (1992), or Hansson-Sandsten (2012).

The EEG figures use de-identified clinical EEG clips (BDSP / ELROND); the data-use is confirmed, so do not flag it, but do check that the clinical description of the seizures is accurate and appropriately hedged.
Two prior tutorials for neuroscientists (Babadi & Brown 2014; Prerau et al. 2017) are the comparison point for exposition; the paper aims to be read alongside them.

Figure captions are in the LaTeX source; figures themselves are PNGs generated by demos/make_figures.py (fig9 = Fig 1 graphical abstract, fig0b = Fig 2, fig0a = Fig 3, fig5 = Fig 4, fig6 = Fig 5, fig8 = Fig 6, fig7 = Fig 7, fig10 = Fig 8, fig11 = Fig 9; supplementary S1-S4 = fig1, fig2, fig3, fig6_full).
